features.name: Browse product catalog
features.description: Allow shoppers to discover and browse a curated collection of handmade products.
acceptance_criteria: The home page introduces the store and provides a clear path to browse products.
The catalog displays multiple products with an image, name, price, and short description or category.
Selecting a product opens its corresponding detail page.
If category filtering is provided, shoppers can clear the filter to return to the full catalog.
Unknown product URLs display a helpful not-found state with a path back to shopping.
verification: Navigate from the home page to the catalog.
Confirm multiple product cards display meaningful content.
Open a product and verify its details correspond to the selected card.
Open an invalid product URL and verify the not-found state.

features.name: View and configure products
features.description: Allow shoppers to understand product details and select valid options before adding products to the cart.
acceptance_criteria: A product detail page displays its name, price, description, images, and availability.
Products with variants expose their relevant options, such as size, color, or finish.
Selecting a variant updates the displayed price when that variant has a price adjustment.
Products supporting personalization display an optional text field with a clear character limit or validation rule.
Required options must be selected before a product can be added to the cart.
Unavailable variants cannot be added to the cart, and their unavailable state is communicated clearly.
The selected variant and personalization are preserved when the product is added to the cart.
The page remains usable on narrow mobile screens without horizontal page overflow.
verification: Select multiple variants and check their displayed prices.
Test a product that supports personalization and one that does not.
Attempt to add a product without selecting a required option.
Attempt to add an unavailable variant.
Verify that the chosen configuration appears correctly in the cart.

features.name: Manage shopping cart
features.description: Allow shoppers to review configured products and modify their cart before checkout.
acceptance_criteria: Shoppers can add valid product configurations to the cart.
Each cart item displays its product name, selected options, applicable personalization, unit price, quantity, and line total.
The line total equals unit price multiplied by quantity.
The subtotal equals the sum of all line totals.
Shoppers can change quantities and remove items.
Quantity cannot be reduced below one through the quantity control; removing an item is a separate action.
Different variants or personalization values remain distinguishable as separate configurations.
Identical configurations may combine into one cart line with an increased quantity.
An empty cart displays a helpful message and a path back to the catalog.
Cart contents persist during navigation, and browser-local persistence is acceptable.
verification: Add a product and confirm it appears in the cart.
Add a second configuration of the same product and verify the configurations remain distinguishable.
Change a quantity and verify the line total and subtotal update.
Remove an item and verify the cart count and subtotal update.
Navigate away from the cart and return to confirm the cart state is preserved.

features.name: Complete simulated checkout
features.description: Demonstrate a complete order journey without collecting payment information or processing a real payment.
acceptance_criteria: Checkout is unavailable when the cart is empty.
The checkout form collects full name, email, address, city, state or region, postal code, and country.
Required fields and email format are validated with clear, actionable messages.
Form values remain available when validation fails.
The checkout summary displays the ordered items and internally consistent totals.
The interface clearly states that checkout is simulated and no payment will be collected.
The checkout does not request payment-card details or make real payment API calls.
Submitting valid details creates a demo order and displays an order reference and summary.
The cart is cleared after successful demo order creation.
Revisiting an order confirmation does not create a duplicate order.
verification: Attempt to access checkout with an empty cart.
Submit incomplete details and verify the validation messages.
Complete checkout with valid details and verify the order confirmation.
Verify the confirmation matches the cart contents and totals.
Confirm the cart is cleared after successful submission.
Inspect the implementation for payment-card fields and real payment calls.

features.name: Display order confirmation
features.description: Show a clear summary of the simulated order after checkout.
acceptance_criteria: The confirmation page displays a unique order reference.
The page displays ordered products, selected options, personalization where applicable, quantities, and totals.
The page clearly identifies the order as a demo.
The page provides a path back to shopping.
Unknown order references display a helpful not-found state.
Refreshing a valid confirmation does not create another order.
verification: Complete a demo order and inspect its confirmation.
Refresh the confirmation page and verify the order remains consistent.
Open an invalid order reference and verify the not-found state.

features.name: Provide a polished, accessible interface
features.description: Deliver a visually coherent storefront that works across common screen sizes and supports basic accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: The layout works at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
Navigation and primary actions are keyboard accessible.
Form fields have visible labels or accessible names.
Interactive elements have visible focus states.
Text and controls have readable contrast and reasonable sizing.
Informative images have meaningful alternative text; decorative images use empty alternative text.
Important state changes, such as cart updates and form errors, are communicated clearly.
The visual design feels consistent across the home, catalog, product, cart, checkout, and confirmation pages.
verification: Inspect the main pages at representative mobile and desktop widths.
Navigate the primary shopping journey using the keyboard.
Check form labels, focus states, image alternative text, and validation feedback.
Review consistency of typography, spacing, color, and interactive states.

features.name: Publish a returns and refunds policy
features.change_request: CR-001: Add a return and refund page
features.description: Give shoppers a clear, findable explanation of how returns, exchanges and refunds work before and after they buy.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated returns and refunds page exists and is reachable from the site footer on every page.
The page states the return window, item condition requirements, how to start a return, refund method and timing, who pays return shipping, and how damaged or incorrect items are handled.
The page states that personalized items are final sale unless they arrive damaged or incorrect.
Products that support personalization tell shoppers, near the personalization field, that personalized pieces are final sale.
The cart or checkout links to the returns policy.
The page clearly states that this is a sample policy for a demo store and that no real returns are processed.
verification: Open the returns page from the footer.
Confirm each policy element is present.
Confirm the final-sale note appears on a personalizable product and not on others.
Follow the returns link from the cart.

features.name: Provide a footer with help, contact and payment information
features.change_request: CR-002: Add a subfooter with payment types accepted and contact us and help links
features.description: Every page ends with a consistent footer and subfooter that lets shoppers find help, contact the studio and see which payment methods the store accepts.
acceptance_criteria: Every page shows the same footer with links to Help & FAQ, Returns & refunds and Contact us.
A subfooter lists accepted payment methods as text labels with accessible names; no third-party card-brand logos are reproduced.
The subfooter makes clear that payment methods are shown for a demo and that checkout does not collect payment.
Help & FAQ and Contact us links lead to real pages, not placeholders.
The Help page answers common questions about shipping, returns, personalization, care and the demo checkout.
The Contact page lists ways to reach the studio and expected response time, and does not submit or transmit messages.
The footer and subfooter work at mobile widths without horizontal overflow.
verification: Check the footer on home, product, cart and checkout pages.
Follow each footer link and confirm the destination page loads.
Confirm payment methods have accessible text and no brand logos.
Inspect the footer at 375 px wide.

features.name: Browsing pages use the full width of the screen
features.change_request: CR-003: Online stores should occupy full width
features.description: Home, catalog and product pages, the header and the footer fill the browser width (to a very large maximum) instead of sitting in a narrow centered column. Reading-heavy pages (cart, checkout, policies, help, contact, order confirmation) keep a narrower column so lines stay readable.
acceptance_criteria: At 1440 px wide, the catalog grid spans at least 90% of the viewport.
The catalog shows more products per row as the screen widens (2, 3, 4, 5, then 6 columns).
Header, footer and page content share the same left and right edges on browsing pages.
Text-heavy pages keep a readable line length.
No horizontal overflow at 375 px.
verification: Measure the catalog grid width against the viewport at 1440 px.
Count columns at several widths.
Check the policy and checkout pages are still narrower than the catalog.

features.name: Product cards put the image first
features.change_request: CR-004: Cards should maximize for image over whitespace
features.description: Product cards give the picture as much of the card as possible: no frame or padding around the image, tight gaps between cards, and a compact text block (category, name, one-line tagline, price).
acceptance_criteria: The product image fills the full width of its card with no border or inner padding.
Image area is at least 70% of the card's height.
Gaps between cards are no more than 16 px on desktop.
Cards remain a single click target with one keyboard tab stop.
verification: Measure image height against card height on the catalog page.
Measure the gap between cards.
Tab through the catalog and confirm one stop per card.

features.name: Home page reassurance strip above the footer
features.change_request: CR-005: Just above the footer, add a similar section on the home page
features.description: The last section of the home page is a row of four reassurances, each with an icon, a short heading and one or two lines: named makers, returns, shipping and contact. It uses only terms this store really has, and its numbers are read from the same settings checkout uses.
acceptance_criteria: The strip is the last section on the home page, directly above the footer.
It shows four items, each with an icon, a heading and a short description.
The returns item states the 30-day window and links to the returns page.
The shipping item states the free-shipping threshold and the flat rate below it, labelled as a demo estimate, and the values match checkout.
The contact item states the two-business-day reply time and links to the contact page.
Four across on wide screens, two across on tablets, one column on phones, with no horizontal overflow at 375 px.
Icons are decorative (hidden from assistive technology) and no claim is made about years trading or customer counts.
verification: Scroll to the bottom of the home page and count the items.
Compare the shipping and returns wording with the Help page and checkout totals.
Resize to 1440, 700 and 390 px.

out_of_scope: Real payment processing or collection of payment-card information
